pick.counterargument: The honest counterargument is the sample: this process has not been shown to work, and a single ranking position is not evidence about one company.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +5.1%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $177.90 on the decision date.
risks: The share count is from 2026-10-22, 34 days older than the price, so the market capitalisation carries that staleness.
The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-10-22, 34 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-11-25.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2026-01-28) plus 364 days

pick.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
pick.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.title: Android’s DIY widgets are a bit of vibe-coding fun
stories.excerpt: Aside from dealing with my calendar, there's one thing I want AI to do: tell me if I'm about to miss the bus. What I need is a widget. It needs to tell me real-time arrivals for the bus stop near my house. Tapping around on my phone screen to open the right app and […]
stories.lead: What I need is a widget. It needs to tell me real-time arrivals for the bus stop near my house. Tapping around on my phone screen to open the right app and select my stop will slow me down enough to miss a bus. I need glanceable information, and I hoped that Android’s vibe-coded widget feature could help me out here. It hasn’t, to my disappointment, but I still had a good time cooking up other widgets.

stories.title: Explosion at a school in eastern Afghanistan kills 7, wounds more than 90
stories.excerpt: Local officials said the blast appeared to have originated in a neighboring depot for mining explosives.
stories.lead:
KABUL, Afghanistan — An explosion at a school in the eastern Afghan province of Kunar Saturday killed seven people and wounded more than 90, the province's culture and information director said, adding that the blast appeared to have originated in a neighboring depot for explosives.

Sami ul Haq Bayan said initial information indicated the blast at the school on the outskirts of the provincial capital, Asadabad, occurred due to negligence at the depot storing explosives belonging to mining companies. An investigation into the incident was underway, he said.

Up to 15 of the wounded remain in hospital, while the rest were discharged after treatment, he added.

stories.title: Afghanistan explosion kills 10 students and injures more than 100, official says
stories.excerpt: A spokesman for Afghanistan's interior ministry says the blast was caused by carelessness at an explosives depot nearby.
stories.lead:
At least 10 students have been killed and 110 others have been injured following an explosion near a school in Afghanistan, a spokesperson has told the BBC.

The incident happened on Saturday morning in the Anderseir area of Asadabad, the capital of Kunar province, the spokesperson for the Taliban government's interior ministry said.

Posting on X, Abdul Mateen Qani said that according to initial investigations, the blast was caused by "negligence and carelessness" at an explosives depot belonging to nearby mining companies.

stories.title: Argentina's bid to stop Falklands oil drilling rejected
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between UK-Israeli companies is set to start exploring for oil and gas, but Argentina sought to block it as part of its claim to sovereignty.
stories.lead:
Argentina's bid to block an oil exploration project near the Falkland Islands has been rejected by a UN-backed international tribunal.

The Argentinian government had called for the venture to be blocked as it claimed there was an ongoing dispute over the sovereignty of the Falklands, a British overseas territory. The UK has repeatedly rejected Argentina's claim.

Speaking on Saturday, the president of the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea said it was the wrong court to rule on questions of sovereignty. The decision was upheld in a vote 18-3.

stories.title: New wave of Democratic attorneys general may reshape the justice system
stories.excerpt: The Democratic victories could have major effects for what alleged crimes are investigated, lawsuits filed and court cases heard across the U.S.
stories.lead:
The nation's legal landscape is set for a major shift after voters elected Democrats to serve as attorney general in five formerly Republican-led states. That means a majority of states will soon have a Democrat serving as the top law enforcement officer.

Democratic candidates flipped attorneys general offices in Georgia, Iowa, Kansas, Ohio and Texas–and in Alaska, the incoming Democratic governor announced his pick for attorney general in a state previously run by Republicans.

stories.lead: It is a fresh Friday afternoon at Selhurst Park and, after posing for a couple of pictures in front of the red and blue Holmesdale End, Jørgen Strand Larsen holds a scarf overhead in true new-signing style. This is not the last step before a routine announcement, nor is this a run-of-the-mill club, his manicured moustache a giveaway. The Crystal Palace and Norway striker has joined forces with Prostate Cancer UK to raise awareness of the disease after his father, Atle Wester, was given a terminal diagnosis this year.

stories.title: Will 2024 version of Palmer ever re-emerge for Chelsea?
stories.excerpt: Cole Palmer's dip in form mirrors Chelsea's recent slump and his frustration was evident after his side's recent defeat against Leeds - but will he ever get back to his best?
stories.lead:
Cole Palmer left the City Ground without having a shot or a touch in the opposition box as Chelsea lost 3-2 at Nottingham Forest on Friday night.

The 24-year-old forward started the season by registering six goal involvements in his first six league games (two goals and four assists), with his penalty against Manchester United now his only goal contribution in the past six matches.

Last weekend, after his side were booed off following the 4-1 defeat by Leeds United, Palmer appeared reluctant to take part in the customary post-match acknowledgement of the supporters.
